name: The Clash
hook: The punk band that kept letting other people's music in, which is why they lasted.
blurb: Most punk bands played fast and stopped there. The Clash covered a Jamaican song on their first album and then hired the man who produced it to produce them. Over six years they absorbed reggae, dub, rockabilly and eventually hip-hop, and that openness is why their records still sound alive. They are the hinge on this map between rock and dub. Their interest in Jamaican music was not tourism: it came from what multiracial West London actually sounded like in the mid-1970s, and it ran through Rock Against Racism, a political movement as much as a musical one.

signatureTracks.title: Police and Thieves
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: A punk band covering a Lee Perry production, six minutes long, on a punk debut album.

signatureTracks.title: Complete Control
